source.title: Sparse but Wrong: Incorrect L0 Leads to Incorrect Features in Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some URLs and words are line-wrapped in the extracted text.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests how SAE feature geometry and sparse-probing results change with L0, and argues that incorrectly chosen L0 produces mixed rather than disentangled SAE latents. It refines claims about SAE feature recovery, but does not test the original toy-network superposition mechanism.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses the Linear Representation Hypothesis and cites prior work on superposition, but those statements are not results of this study. Reported L0 sweeps and feature-mixing results are included below. The toy-model MSE comparison (2.73 for the trained SAE versus 4.88 for the ground-truth SAE) concerns reconstruction rather than feature identity, so it is not cataloged as a separate version-specific row. Figures 20–22 and the search of open-source SAEs are not rows because they do not apply, measure, or test the claimed representation behavior.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs at varied L0 on toy data with known features and on Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.2-1b. It shows learned latents mix true features unless L0 is correct. This bears on whether dictionary features are stable, canonical units (V5). It assumes rather than tests the LLM superposition premise (V4).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. It should add three points. The authors argue sparsity–reconstruction tradeoff plots are misleading, since correct dictionaries reconstruct worse at low L0. They support low-L0 mixing with a theoretical proof. And they say most open-source SAEs (L0 < 100) are likely set too low.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than reproducing Toy Models of Superposition, the study trains BatchTopK and JumpReLU SAEs on synthetic feature data and LLM activations, varying SAE L0 and measuring feature correspondence, decoder geometry, and sparse-probing performance.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes change with SAE L0, SAE architecture (BatchTopK versus JumpReLU), model and layer, toy-feature correlations, SAE width, and whether training starts below or above the target L0. The cdec minimum is broad in some settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Decoder pairwise cosine similarity (cdec) is minimized at the true L0 in toy BatchTopK, JumpReLU and superposition-noise SAEs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoder geometry can diagnose a mis-set SAE sparsity level.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: LLM feature identity is not known, so LLM results rely on decoder-geometry proxies and sparse-probing benchmarks rather than ground-truth feature comparisons. Only a few layers of popular LLMs are evaluated. The authors report broad cdec minima in some cases and imperfect correlation with sparse-probing performance, particularly at high L0. The transition and automatic L0-selection results also have stated local-minimum or hyperparameter-tuning concerns.
record.rows_left_out: Appendix D's additional correlation-strength and fine-grained L0 sweeps (Figures 12–14), Appendix E's detailed feature-cosine plots (Figures 15 and 17), and Figure 20–22 analyses were not given separate rows. They are auxiliary sweeps or summaries of SAE L0/threshold distributions rather than distinct tests needed for the version verdicts; key toy width/noise and LLM findings are retained in r26–r27 and r12–r25.

untested.parts: The main toy models use orthogonal features with d > g. The superposition-noise variants do not examine the geometry, the sparsity-dependent transition, or how features are stored.
Not tested: no analysis of why neurons are polysemantic or of capacity allocation.
Not tested: no analysis of non-capacity causes of neuron polysemanticity.
The study assumes that LLM activations are sums of sparse linear features. Sparse-probing F1 has no dense or neuron baseline, so it does not show that LLMs contain recoverable sparse features.
The study assumes linear 1-D features and explicitly leaves non-linear features aside (Appendix A).

missing.what: Theorems F.1 and F.2: when K is below the true L0, the disentangled SAE is not even a local minimum of expected MSE. This is a specific argument against SAE latents being canonical.
Trained L0=1 and L0=5 SAEs beat the ground-truth SAE on MSE despite heavily polysemantic latents. MSE 2.73 vs 4.88 at L0=5. Bears on whether reconstruction-optimal dictionaries are the true units.
Mixing scales with correlation strength, is zero at zero correlation, and grows as L0 moves below the true L0 (1.7–2.0). It persists under superposition noise.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 links on the LLM rows were removed. The study presupposes sparse linear features in LLMs and measures SAE quality as a function of L0, so those rows bear on V5. Row states were normalized so that each is judged against V5 holding, meaning latents correspond to true features. The proxy-validation rows (r10, r11, r26) were moved to fits_no_version. The study is not an original source for any version.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether an underlying network with more sparse features than dimensions stores them as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, or whether that geometry has the claimed sparsity-dependent transition.
The study examines SAE latents, not whether LLM neurons become polysemantic because important features receive dedicated dimensions while other features share them.
It does not test other causes of polysemanticity in LLM neurons or whether polysemanticity alone is evidence of superposition.

LLM evidence is indirect: sparse-probing performance and decoder-geometry proxies are measured, not ground-truth recovery of LLM features. The study covers only selected models, layers, SAE architectures, and training distributions.

The study tests whether SAE features vary with L0 and can mix underlying features. It does not establish whether there is a unique canonical dictionary, whether features are complete, or whether they are stable across training seeds and other choices.
It does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features as alternative units of superposition.

relationships.condition: Toy SAEs (5- and 50-feature, known ground truth) trained at L0 below or above the true L0, or started too low
relationships.reason: Latents mix correlated and anti-correlated true features when L0 is wrong. Starting too low leaves many incorrect features even after L0 is corrected (r1, r3, r5, r7, r9).
